items.title: New discount warehouse is bringing bargain shopping to Mississauga and Oakville
items.summary: A large discount warehouse is opening near the Mississauga border next month, promising 30,000 square feet of deals on household goods, personal care products, kitchen appliances and other merchandise. Clearance Warehouse has announced plans to open its new Oakville location on Nov. m. , at the corner of Ford Drive and Royal Windsor Drive, in the former RONA building. The location is expected to draw bargain hunters from Oakville and neighbouring Mississauga, with the company promoting discounts of up to 80 per cent off retail prices. Unlike a traditional retail store, Clearance Warehouse operates through limited-time sales featuring liquidation, overstock and closeout merchandise. Inventory can change between sales, giving shoppers a rotating selection of products and deals. Merchandise typically includes kitchenware, small appliances, bedding, household cleaning supplies, health and beauty products, clothing, tools and seasonal items. The company does not sell its merchandise online, meaning shoppers must visit the warehouse in person to browse and purchase available products. Clearance Warehouse already operates locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, and its return to Oakville brings another option to bargain hunters in the western GTA. m. m. m. m.

items.title: House of the week: Custom-built home that backs on to creek in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A custom-built home that backs onto a creek in Mississauga. Features: This custom-built home is located in Lakeview. Rebuilt from the foundation up with a substantial addition, the home offers over 5,000 square feet of finished space. The heart of the home is a Cambria kitchen with stainless steel built-in appliances and an island, all flowing into the family room. The open-concept layout is highlighted by a ballroom-style living/dining area featuring 15-foot ceilings. Features include four bedrooms, seven washrooms and a fully self-contained basement apartment with a separate entrance. There is also an office, recreational room and additional washroom in the basement. The home is set on a large lot backing directly onto Etobicoke Creek. Find landscaped gardens, a composite deck, a stone patio and walkways outside. The property is near two golf courses, parks, waterfront trails, major highways, transit, shopping and amenities. Thanks to Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage for all the information about the House of the Week. For more information about this house, please visit Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage.

items.title: Haunted Mississauga Tour brings 190-year-old political rivalries back to life
items.summary: A Halloween-season tradition returns to Mississauga this month, giving residents a chance to explore the city’s past on a nighttime tour filled with historical characters, political rivalries, and a few spooky surprises. The 25th annual Haunted Mississauga Heritage Tour takes place Friday, Oct. 23, at Streetsville Memorial Cemetery, where visitors will be transported back to 1836 to experience a turbulent chapter in Upper Canada’s political history. Organized by Heritage Mississauga, the event uses live, unscripted theatrical performances to bring the past to life, with volunteer performers portraying historical characters and events as visitors make their way through the cemetery. This year’s production focuses on the 1836 election in Upper Canada, a period when political loyalties ran deep and elections could turn dangerous. The theme, described as “Axe Handles & Whiskey,” offers a glimpse into a time when political disputes could involve more than heated words. Rather than a traditional haunted house, the experience combines local history, storytelling and Halloween atmosphere, with performances unfolding throughout the guided cemetery walk. Haunted Mississauga traces its origins to 2002, when an event featuring the late author Terry Boyle, who wrote Haunted Ontario, proved popular enough to inspire the creation of the annual tours. The event has since become a recurring opportunity to explore the stories and characters that shaped the city’s past. The tour takes place outdoors after dark at Streetsville Memorial Cemetery, located at 299 Queen St. S. m. Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes. Admission is listed at $5 for adults, with limited spaces available.

items.title: What you should know about endorsements for Mississauga, Brampton municipal elections
items.summary: Recognizable labour unions and special interest groups concerned about everything from jobs to municipal service levels are backing campaigns and helping candidates make public their positions on key election issues. Mississauga mayoral hopeful Alvin Tedjo was endorsed by the Peel Regional Police Association in Mississauga on Sept. 21. The association has endorsed Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown and federal candidates before, but not a Mississauga mayoral candidate. As public safety, crime and police budgets draw political discussion during Brampton and Mississauga municipal election campaigning, the Peel police union has very publicly thrown its support behind some candidates. The Peel Regional Police Association (PRPA) is the labour union for about 4,000 Peel Regional Police (PRP) officers and civilian staff. It previously endorsed candidates in the 2018 municipal and 2025 federal elections. Peel Regional Police Association president Adrian Woolley told Metroland Media the union can and will endorse candidates they see as “strong advocates” for community safety. “We’re able to and going to endorse anyone that is down for making sure that community safety is a priority and making sure that my members are looked after,” PRPA president Adrian Woolley told Metroland Media. As the Oct. 26 vote nears, the PRPA is among a number of organizations and individuals offering public endorsements for Brampton and Mississauga candidates perceived as looking out for their interests. Randy Besco, an elections and public opinion expert at the University of Toronto said endorsements might change election outcomes to a small extent but mostly, people don’t pay close attention to them.

items.title: Peel Police Investigate After Car Carrying Two People Hits Mississauga Bus Shelter
items.summary: According to Insauga, a vehicle crashed into a bus shelter in Mississauga on Friday morning, leaving the structure collapsed and glass scattered across the sidewalk. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet the vehicle, which was occupied by a driver and one passenger, struck the shelter on Oct. 9. Police said the investigation into the collision and the circumstances surrounding it remains ongoing. Photos from the scene show a silver vehicle resting on the sidewalk next to the destroyed shelter. Insauga reports this isn't the first time a bus shelter in Peel Region has been hit by a vehicle, pointing to a September 2024 multi-vehicle crash at Derry Road West and Terragar Boulevard in Meadowvale West that left one pedestrian with minor injuries. The outlet also noted a June crash this year in which a bus shelter was destroyed and a light pole damaged after one driver fled the scene.

items.title: Peel Police Called In After Man Tries to Jump Costco Pokemon Card Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police were called to a Mississauga Costco near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street early Friday morning after a man tried to cut into a lineup forming ahead of a new Pokemon card release. Social media posts had circulated word that Costco Canada's Ascended Heroes Mini Tin 5-Packs were expected to drop at select stores on Oct. 9, including the Laird Road location in Mississauga and a Newmarket store. Insauga reports officers were brought in to help manage the crowd that gathered in anticipation of the release. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet officers were on a paid duty assignment monitoring the lineup when one person reportedly tried to take a spot ahead of others waiting. Insauga reports the incident reflects the lengths some collectors will go to secure sought-after Pokemon card products as demand for new releases continues to drive early-morning crowds at retailers.

items.title: Mississauga Man's Three Decades of Playing the Lottery Finally Pay Off With $500K Lump Sum
items.summary: According to Insauga, Dennis, a 50-year-old Mississauga man who has played the lottery for about 30 years, is weighing what to do with a windfall after winning big through the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation. OLG says Dennis matched all five main numbers in the Sept. 3 Daily Grand draw to win the second prize of $25,000 a year for life, and chose a lump-sum payment of $500,000 instead of the annuity. Dennis told OLG the experience felt truly out of this world and that the feeling was unreal. He said he picked up coffee, had breakfast at home and decided to check his tickets before realizing what had happened, recalling that he could not process it at first. While collecting his winnings at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto, Dennis said he told his mother first, and that she thought he was joking until it sank in. Insauga reports Dennis plans to save and invest the money for the future rather than rush into any major decisions.

items.title: A Creemore Jail Visit Leads Modern Mississauga Writer to a 19th-Century Local Land Deal
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent road trip to Collingwood turned into an unexpected history lesson when the writer stopped in Creemore and visited what's reportedly the smallest jail in North America, the Little Lock-up, built in 1894. Nearby stands Claverleigh, a National Historic Site built in 1871 as a rectory for Reverend William Rabbath Forster, who also directed construction of Creemore's St. Luke's Anglican Church in 1887. The outlet reports Forster purchased 100 acres in Lot 32, Concession 2, north of Dundas Street, on May 24, 1850, shortly after arriving in Canada, and sold the property to his brother Frederick Forster in 1855. That same parcel of land in historic Mississauga is where Millennium Grove and Dunn Park now sit along Erin Mills Parkway, north of Burnhamthorpe Road. Modern Mississauga Media says the find was one of several unexpected connections back to Mississauga turned up during the writer's meandering road trip north.

items.title: Open Ward 7 Council Seat Draws Field of 17 After Incumbent Enters Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, 17 candidates are competing for Ward 7's open council seat after sitting councillor Dipika Damerla left to run for mayor in the Oct. 26 municipal election. The outlet said candidates who didn't respond to its questionnaire had their information pulled from the City of Mississauga's certified candidates list instead. One candidate highlighted a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, including time managing neighbourhood safety programs, and said growing up in Mississauga shaped a lasting connection to the city. That candidate said priorities include improving community safety through data-informed engagement strategies that bring Peel police, non-profits and the city together, along with building up resident associations to give tenants and condo residents a stronger voice. Mississauga.com reports the crowded Ward 7 race reflects a broader reshuffling of council as Damerla's mayoral run opened up one of the city's most contested seats.
